provenance_note: Hand-derived from 732.1-B-3 §4.1.2 (the Primary Header), §4.1.3, §4.1.4.1.5-12 (OID frames), §4.1.5, §6.3, §4.2.8-4.2.11 and docs/04-engines.md §2.3 (LNK-030…LNK-036), OI-68; UPIDs from specs/sana/uslp_protocol_id.tsv. Model test-vectors/models/link_send.py, written blind (TV-023) by a Claude agent from the Blue Books and docs/ only, without reading any implementation. The input scripts were chosen by hand; the expected outputs are the model's. The file is written by the model (--write) and never edited by hand.

scenarios.description: With no VC offering, an OID frame: VCID 63, MAP ID 0, rule 001, UPID Only Idle Data, Last Valid Octet Pointer at the last TFDZ octet, the TFDZ from the OID generator, which continues; no VCF Count by default on VCID 63.
An OID frame with a VCF Count Length of 2 for VCID 63: the mux counts OID frames like any VC; the count has the configured length.

Sequence-controlled and expedited frames of a VC are counted separately, each with the VCF Count Length of its QoS (2 and 1 octets on VC 1, so the TFDF is 1 octet longer for expedited frames); the Bypass Flag is set for expedited.
A VCF Count Length of 1 octet: the count wraps modulo 256 after 255 (257 frames of VC 1).
The MAP ID of a frame is the one the offer names (or the VC's); VC 2 carries MAP 3; the VC Frame Count is per VC, not per MAP.
VC 1 requires an OCF in every frame (the OCF Flag is set); VC 2 has none; the OID frame has one because the entry for VCID 63 says so, and it is a expedited-QoS frame.
An Insert Zone of 2 octets in every frame, the OID frame included; a frame with no new IN_SDU repeats the slot and is followed by Notify(InsertSduRepeated) (OI-68).
A 3-octet Security Header and a 2-octet Security Trailer on VC 1: they surround the TFDF (6.3.5); the action gives their ranges and the range of the TFDF.
Round robin applies to a USLP channel as to the others: VC 1 and VC 2 alternate.
